title: Tyre Strategy
statement:
You are the race strategist. The race has `L` laps and there are `C` tyre compounds. Compound `i` has base time `b`, degradation `d` and a maximum stint length `m`: the **k-th lap** of a stint on that compound takes `b + d × (k − 1)` ms, and a set can do **at most `m` laps**.

You may pit **any number of times**. Every pit stop costs `P` ms and puts on a fresh set of any compound (the same compound again is allowed).

The rules say a driver must use **at least two different compounds** during the race (if only one compound exists, this rule is ignored).

Print the minimum possible total race time. The input always allows at least one legal strategy.
input_format:
The first line contains `L` and `P`.
The second line contains `C`.
Each of the next `C` lines contains a compound name and three integers `b d m`.
output_format: One integer, the minimum race time in milliseconds.
starter_code:
L, P = map(int, input().split())
C = int(input())
compounds = []
for _ in range(C):
    name, b, d, m = input().split()
    compounds.append((int(b), int(d), int(m)))

# your code here
notes: Hint: think about the best time to finish the first `i` laps with a given set of compounds used so far.
